applies_why: This judge text does the thing K-S2 governs because it labels Isaiah 7:14 UNDERDETERMINED on the ground that different sides answered different senses/aspects of that single verse.
quote: D5 vs C5 (Isaiah 7:14): UNDERDETERMINED -- Challenger answered the virgin and young-woman wording in [DR3] and defender answered the prophetic application in [CR2] and [CR3].
rule_words: That a single verse does not state a link or its contrary is never a ground for STANDS or UNDERDETERMINED, for either side. A verse that carries two senses at once is not open. Both senses stand.
room: the phrase 'A verse that carries two senses at once is not open'; readings weighed: (1) the virgin/young-woman wording and prophetic application are two senses at once, so UNDERDETERMINED is forbidden, or (2) they are merely separate arguments/rounds, so the two-senses clause would not directly apply.
why: The judge treats Isaiah 7:14 as open/UNDERDETERMINED because different sides answered the virgin/young-woman wording and the prophetic application, but K-S2 says a verse carrying two senses at once is not open and both senses stand.
